name: odin_accelerated_time
description: ODIN saturated at its maximum SOP rate: 75 MHz clock, r_SOP = f_clk/2 = 37.5 MSOP/s, 0.55 V. The census needs no activity assumption -- the architecture fixes it. This is the point E_SOP was measured at, so it checks that Eq. (2) is assembled correctly; the biological-time case is the one that shows it generalizes.

census_sources.neurons_used: every neuron is updated on each event: 'all N neurons of ODIN will be updated'
census_sources.tiles: a single core, so a single tile
census_sources.segment_cores: the one core is configured once
census_sources.sync_count: a single core has nothing to synchronize across
census_sources.timesteps: one 1-second window at the stated SOP rate, so mJ per window = mW
census_sources.latency_steps: one 1-second window at the stated SOP rate
census_sources.synaptic_events: the published SOP rate r_SOP for this operating point, over one second
census_sources.host_macs: a bare-chip characterization: no host ComputeOps
census_sources.host_ops_s: a bare-chip characterization: no host wall

average_power_mw.quote: At a clock frequency of 75MHz, the maximum rSOP is equal to 37.5MSOP/s and the measured power consumption P of ODIN is 477uW at 0.55V
